verification.wordpress_plugin_check: one WARNING repaired, 2026-09-05: WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.InterpolatedNotPrepared in the chat logger. Five PluginCheck.CodeAnalysis.AIProvider.DirectIntegration warnings remain and are design, not defect — see plugin_check_ai_provider_note.

v3_fixes: Recovered answer no longer shown twice after a signed-in reload mid-response.
profile_hash computed on read when the stored field is empty, so the chat log column is never blank.
Chat log export filename carries a full MTS to the millisecond instead of the date alone.
v4_fixes: The framework no longer claims membership grants 'full access to all content'.
A personality built in the builder opens with the same header the shipped ones do.
The portability line moved to the download; provenance is visible beside the profile.
The site index reads whichever post types the flow selects, not only 'post'.
BuddyBoss group directory indexed, catalogued on every turn, and fail-closed by tier and group privacy.
The compiled profile is sent on every turn, not only the first. Recorded here after the fact: it shipped in v4 and was first written up in v5.
plugin_check_ai_provider_note: Plugin Check suggests WordPress 7.0 wp_ai_client_prompt() wherever it sees a provider hostname. The five flagged lines are the model-catalog and model-detail endpoints, which enumerate what a floscAdmin key can use so the admin dropdown shows real models. The AI Client sends prompts; it does not list a provider catalogue for a key, so the suggested replacement does not cover these calls. Left visible rather than annotated away. Adopting the AI Client for the prompt path is a real feature decision, not a lint fix.
v5_fixes: A personality can be renamed. state.soul.name was read in six places in the builder — the profile heading, the identity line, the save payload and four export filenames — and written in none. No field existed, so the name seeded from the library at boot was the only name a personality could ever have. Same for the role. The id is untouched: it is the key a flow attaches by.

The chat logger quotes its table name with a %i placeholder instead of interpolating it into the SQL string (Plugin Check, WordPress.DB.PreparedSQL.InterpolatedNotPrepared), and check_log_contract.php now fails on any line that interpolates it.
